newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Deutsche Bank gives up Brazil power appeal.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank gives up Brazil power appeal.

text.p: A consortium led by Deutsche Bank has withdrawn its appeal of a decision to award a group led by a local bank a contract to advise on the privatization of two Brazilian power generators, the government said.

Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) also said in a statement it plans to sign the so-called B service contract for the sale of Furnas and Eletrosul with the Banco Graphus-led consortium next week.
The B service contract calls for the group to provide a financial and economic evaluation and draft a privatization model.
Eletrosul and Furnas are units of federal power holding Eletrobras.

Earlier this month, the BNDES awarded the B contract to the Graphus-led group and an A service contract, consisting of a financial and economic evaluation as well as a technical and operational analysis, to the Deutsche Bank led group.
The price asked by the winning consortium for A service was 1.49 million reais while the B service contract went for $1.92 million, the BNDES said.
